title: Christmas Tree Swirl Cupcakes
shortDescription: Vanilla cupcakes with a tall green frosting swirl and star sprinkle, ready in 43 minutes total.
description: These cupcakes look like little Christmas trees on a plate. I pipe the green frosting tall and narrow, then top each one with a gold star sprinkle. The cake underneath is a simple vanilla base that bakes up soft and moist. It holds a tall swirl without sinking, which matters a lot for this design. I tested this recipe three times in my home kitchen to get the frosting stiff enough for height but still soft to eat. A star tip and steady piping hand are all you need for the tree look.
ingredients: 1 1/2 cups unsalted butter, softened, for frosting
instructions: Preheat oven to 350°F. Line a 12 cup muffin pan with paper liners.
Whisk flour, baking powder, and salt in a bowl. Set aside.
Beat butter and sugar together for 3 minutes until light and fluffy.
Add eggs one at a time, mixing well after each. Stir in vanilla.
Add the flour mix in three parts, alternating with milk. Mix just until smooth.
Divide batter evenly among liners, filling each about two thirds full.
Bake 16 to 18 minutes, until a toothpick comes out clean. Cool fully on a wire rack.
Beat butter for the frosting until smooth, about 2 minutes.
Add powdered sugar one cup at a time, then mix in cream and vanilla.
Add green gel coloring a little at a time until you reach a deep pine green.
Fit a piping bag with a star tip. Pipe from the outer edge inward, building tall layered rings up to a peak.
Top each swirl with a star sprinkle while the frosting is still soft.
tips: Chill the frosting for 10 minutes if it feels too soft to hold height.
Use a closed star tip like Wilton 1M for the clearest tree ridges.
Pipe in one steady spiral motion. Do not stop halfway or the tree will look uneven.
Bake cupcakes a day ahead and frost them the day you plan to serve.

faq.question: Why is my frosting swirl not holding its tall shape?
faq.answer: Your frosting is too soft. Chill it in the fridge for 10 minutes and beat it again briefly before piping.

faq.question: Can I make the frosting green without gel coloring?
faq.answer: Liquid food coloring works but you need more of it, which can thin the frosting. Gel keeps the texture stiff for tall swirls.

faq.question: How far ahead can I frost these cupcakes?
faq.answer: Frost them up to 6 hours before serving. Store at room temperature away from heat so the swirl stays firm.

faq.question: What piping tip gives the best tree texture?
faq.answer: A large closed star tip, like a Wilton 1M or 2D, creates the ridged branch look in one smooth pull.

conclusion: These cupcakes turn a simple vanilla base into a festive holiday centerpiece. The tall green swirl and star sprinkle make them look far fancier than the effort they take. Bring them to your next holiday party and watch them disappear first.
